author: Mark Atwood
text:
Items 5, 6, 9, 16 and 1 now also closed. Only the heading-style call is left, and that is yours to make.

1. Verified closed, not taken on trust. pkix-aia-http's rustdoc now carries the full non-public address list (RFC 6598 shared space, 0.0.0.0/8, 240.0.0.0/4, IPv6 site-local, the IPv4-mapped / IPv4-compatible / NAT64 forms, and 169.254.169.254 by name), the asymmetry warning, and a reference to pkix-net-guard. Also checked net-guard's claim that aia-http re-exports its resolvers: true, 'pub use pkix_net_guard::GuardedResolver' plus GuardedAsyncResolver.

5. The PKIX-lwr9.4 'design call pending: harness fix vs new pkix-path-builder helper' was answered with BOTH, two baselines back -- lwr9.4.2 added build_first_valid_path and lwr9.4.1 made the limbo loader use it. Marked resolved, kept the diagnosis since it is the only copy of what reframed 47 cases down to one. And the residual list: I first 'corrected' 5 to 4, then checked the JSON -- still 5, but the fifth is rfc5280::nc::permitted-self-issued, which took tc60's place in the same delta. Now named rather than counted.

6. The per-bucket tables had drifted past being merely stale: LooserThanWild listed openssl CRL-expired / cRLSign-missing / CRL-signature-failure rows that no longer occur at all, and missed 9 pyca nameConstraints refusals and 2 pyca revocation findings; StricterThanWild claimed 12 name-constraints and 5 not-a-CA entries that are gone. Both are now GENERATED from baseline-pkits.json with normalised reasons, so they sum exactly to 63 and 56 and cannot drift again. Rewrote the Net paragraph (30 policy-tree / 22 CRL-coverage / 3 revocation / 1 DSA) and the 'Reading this baseline' caveat, which no longer applies to those tables and never applied to the 'What changed in revision X' sections -- those are history and their numbers are deliberately frozen. Also fixed the summary table and ground-truth tally, stale since the delta-CRL fix, and the 4.2.3 diagnosis which blamed 'x509-cert 0.2.5' and 'pre-2000 UTCTime' when the floor is the epoch and the restriction is der's.

9. pkix-chain's enumeration was missing trust-anchor matching and policy mappings; it now points at pkix-path's list rather than keeping a copy that drifts. Its feature table omitted the fact a reader would get wrong -- that crl/ocsp fetch nothing and the caller supplies DER bytes -- which is how pkix-revocation's own table puts it.

16. Resolvable after all: the figure is measured, it was just recorded somewhere nobody looked. pkix-zlint-bridge/tests/enumerate_lints.rs documents 419 lints (353 e_, 55 w_, 11 n_) counted with 'zlint -list-lints-json | jq -r .name | sed s/_.*$// | sort | uniq -c' against zlint dev-unknown on 2026-05-12. So ~400 is right and ~700 was wrong. Both crates now cite the provenance and the version-dependence instead of asserting a bare number.

pkix-zlint-bridge 0.2.2, pkix-policy-zlint 0.2.1.
